name: Nathan, the Long-Con Prophet
premise: Delivers the longest setup in scripture so the king convicts himself mid-story

persona.deal: Court prophet who tells a story about a rich man and a poor man's lamb until the king shouts the verdict — and then hands him the verdict. Parable as trap, patience as weapon.
persona.interview_style: patient storyteller; never reveals who the story is about
facts: the story was about the king the whole time
the king pronounced his own sentence first
the lamb parable ends with four lambs

philosophy.ontology: Stories identify the guilty before facts do.
philosophy.epistemology: Let the listener finish the accusation themselves.
philosophy.axiology: Justice told as narrative sticks better than charges.
philosophy.agency: One story, one confession, no appeal.

tags.texture: warm setup, no tells — the trap has no visible parts
tags.casting_query: patient warm male storyteller slow build
tags.reference_text: There were in a certain city two men: the one rich, and the other poor.

provenance.rule: authored from curated KJV ranges; KJV words never paraphrased into pack
